title: Ordinary tensor localization is natural on homology
statement: Let R,Rp,A,B,D be commutative rings in one universe, with A and B algebras over R and Rp, D algebras over E=A tensor_R B and F=A tensor_Rp B and over B, and compatible scalar towers B→E→D and B→F→D. Choose derived categories of R-,Rp- and B-modules. Let Q be an A-cochain complex, i an integer and L,K base-derived tensor models over R,Rp [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model]. Put CL=E tensor_A Q, CK=F tensor_A Q, TL=D tensor_A Q via E, and TK=D tensor_A Q via F. Let tau:TL≅TK fix d tensor q and let psi between the B-restrictions of CL,CK fix (1 tensor b) tensor q in every degree. For every y in H^i(CL), homology of tau applied to homology of L.ordinaryToLocalized(y), transported through exact restriction E→D, equals homology of K.ordinaryToLocalized applied to homology of psi of y, transported through the inverse B-restriction homology isomorphism of CL and the forward one of CK, then through exact restriction F→D. No base localization hypothesis or comparison/cohomology-of-derived-functor map occurs in the identity.

source.place: Tag 0DJ8, lemma-single-complex-base-change-condition, affine localization identity; More on Algebra, Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change, universal derived tensor comparison.

proof.text: Forget the scalar structures and prove the chain square ordinaryToLocalized(L);tau = forget(psi);ordinaryToLocalized(K). Use surjectivity of L.ordinaryIso in every degree and tensor induction on B tensor_R Q. On b tensor q, use ordinaryIso_tmul, both ordinaryToLocalized_tmul equations, hpsi and htau; the two images of b in D agree by the B scalar-tower equations. Zero and addition cases follow from additivity.

Use the proved forgetHomologyMap and forgetHomologyIso_comp helper API from SemilinearScalarExtensionHomologySquare, and ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso_hom_naturality for psi and tau. The B-restriction homology isomorphisms followed by forgetting equal the direct forgetful homology isomorphisms. Conjugating H(psi) therefore gives exactly the two restriction factors in the displayed formula. Apply homology to the chain square and compose these identities. Cancel the middle exact homology isomorphisms and evaluate at y.
